faq.a: Stories help us remember important things, teach lessons, bond with others and imagine other lives. Every known human culture tells stories.
asks: What is the point of stories?

faq.q: Why do we remember stories better than facts?
faq.a: Stories link facts together with characters, feelings and a sequence of events, which gives the brain more hooks to hold on to. That is why people kept history in stories before writing.

Fables and folk tales hide a lesson inside a fun story, like the tortoise and the hare teaching that slow and steady can win. The Panchatantra from India and Aesop's fables from Greece are famous examples.

faq.q: How do stories bring people together?
faq.a: When people share a story, they laugh, worry and hope together, which builds friendship and a shared identity. Communities often have stories about where they came from.

faq.q: How do stories help us imagine?
faq.a: Stories let us step into other people's lives in our minds, practise feelings safely and picture what might happen. Some research suggests reading fiction can help people understand others' feelings.

facts: A cave painting at Leang Karampuang in Sulawesi, Indonesia, showing human-like figures with a pig, was dated in 2024 to at least 51,200 years old.
The Panchatantra, a collection of animal fables from India, is thought to date from around 300 BCE to 300 CE and has been translated into many languages.

quiz.say: Why did people keep history in stories before writing existed?
quiz.show: Before writing, history was kept in stories because…
quiz.why: Characters, feelings and events help the brain hold on to information.

wrong.1: There was no law about it; stories simply worked.
wrong.2: Stories carried facts in a memorable form.

quiz.say: Where is one of the oldest known picture stories?
quiz.show: One of the oldest picture stories is in…
quiz.why: The Leang Karampuang cave painting is at least 51,200 years old.

wrong.1: Cinemas are only about 130 years old.
wrong.2: Comics are very recent compared with cave art.
